items.text: Medicare enrollment has three windows, not one. IEP: seven months around your 65th birthday, no penalty. GEP: Jan-Mar if you missed it, with one. SEPs: job loss, moves, and more. Not connected with or endorsed by the U.S. government or the federal Medicare program.

Most of the confusion we hear about Medicare enrollment comes down to one thing: people assume there is a single window, and there isn't.

The Initial Enrollment Period, IEP, is tied to turning 65. It runs seven months: three before your birthday month, that month, and three after. No penalty attached.

Miss it without other qualifying coverage, and the fallback is the General Enrollment Period, GEP, which runs January through March every year. The Part B late penalty applies for as long as you have Part B.

Then there are Special Enrollment Periods, SEPs - not one window but a category. Losing employer coverage, moving, and other life events each open their own SEP with its own length and start date.

The mistake we see most: assuming a life change will "obviously" trigger a window, when it either does not qualify or the clock already started.

Worth five minutes to confirm which window you are actually in.
